I am not aware of this decision or anything that it seems to indicate, the setting up of a staff. I did know these people personally, however, and I told you specifically when I met each of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This document alleges that Atif Krdzic, apart from being a member of the Srebrenica TO staff, which I don't want you to comment about, he was also organiser of armed resistance against the aggressor in the area of Osmace. Were you aware of that fact? I think you need to say "Da" or not, because the interpreters need to hear your voice.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The same question with regard to Nedzad Bektic. It is alleged that he was organiser of armed resistance in the area of Kragljevode.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And it's also alleged in this document that Senaid Tabakovic was one of the organisers of armed resistance in the area of Skenderovici.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're aware of these facts. Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Last question: Are you aware that one or more of these names, of these persons mentioned here, functioned as a member of the Srebrenica TO staff?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he has already answered that question. Yes, anyway, if you haven't, please answer it now.

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: I said I didn't know, didn't I? It's before I arrived; therefore, there is nothing I can say about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Let me try again, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's already told us that, for the first period during his stay in Srebrenica, he wasn't even aware of the existence of a so-called Srebrenica TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, of course, and what I asked him, Your Honour, is, is it, according to your experience when you were in Srebrenica, that these persons were functioning at that time as members of the TO staff. That's the question. Not in reverse, earlier in time to May, because he can't testify about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But if he's -- Did you ever, at any time, come to know about the existence of the Srebrenica TO staff? Srebrenica Territorial --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I never came to know about the Srebrenica TO staff. What I said was that there were a group of people, local commanders, these amongst them, who would meet and discuss the ways in which to resist the aggressor. I was never aware of any decision or a formal document at the time to set up a Srebrenica TO staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the only question that you can put to the witness, Mr. Wubben, is whether, to his knowledge, these three persons ever formed part of the staff that he was aware of? Not of the Srebrenica Territorial staff. The staff that he's been continually referring to, this loosely structured -- according to him, because that's how he described it in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Point taken, Your Honour. I will continue with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but you have to ask the question, because it's an important question. You can't ask him whether he -- to his knowledge, they were members of, and participated as members of, the Srebrenica TO staff, because at no time did he come to know of the existence of a so-called Srebrenica TO staff. But he has told us that he is aware that there was a staff at the time. Did these three persons, to your knowledge, form part of that staff, in August, when you arrived? In August of 1992. You told us that there was a staff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I told you is that there was an informal, I'm saying informal, group. I didn't see it as a staff at the time. It was an informal group with local commanders who would come to Srebrenica from as far as 20 or 30 kilometres away. They would come to attend meetings, to deal with certain problems. I'll say it again: I was not aware of the existence of any TO staff, and I also said I wasn't interested, and I also said that my task and my job at the time was quite different on account of which there's nothing I can tell you about the existence of any TO staff that was organised in such and such a way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question, therefore, goes back to what you've just said. This informal gathering, informal group, to your knowledge, did Atif Krdzic belong to that group? Did Nedzad Bektic belong to that group or come for meetings of that group? Did Senaid Tabakovic, I think you told us he already did, belong to that group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I told you when I met those people. I can't speak about August. I said that I met Atif Krdzic late in the year. I heard that there was a commander named Atif Krdzic in the south-east of the Srebrenica area. I didn't even know what the man looked like. I had heard of Nedzad Bektic, but I didn't know what he looked like. I had heard of Senaid Tabakovic. I had no idea what he looked like. I knew he was a local commander in the Skenderovici area. But I only met them one at a time. I didn't have time to go around and meet all these people. I met them when they came to see me, when they brought a problem of their own to the hospital. That's when I met them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Meeting them and coming to know them is one thing. Knowing that they became part of this informal group that you mentioned is another. And My question precisely is whether, to your knowledge, in August of 1992, these three persons, or any one of these three persons, formed part of this informal group? It's not when -- I'm not contesting when you came to know them personally, but it seems that you knew that there was a group, an informal group, in August. I'm asking you whether you knew also that these three persons formed part of that group in August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, okay. Judge Eser has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Just to clarify this point. Now, was it that you just did not know the term of Territorial Defence, or was it -- you had mentioned that there was some informal gatherings, and that these three people belonged to this gathering, where they would come together. Now, you had said so, testified so, on these terms. Now, can you confirm that there was some sort of a group, whatever you call it, at least that there was a group, and that these people, even if you did not know them personally at that time, had been part or taking -- participating in this group?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Can Your Honour please put the question in an open way, because leading questions from the Bench are even worse. Possibly these people were simply coming and going into Srebrenica without belonging -- I'm not even sure if one can belong to a gathering. But if the witness could simply be asked whether -- were these -- a very open position, like did this people come and go occasionally, meet informally, or was there a slightly more formalised group? I'd hate to have a leading question like that coming from the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's already -- the question acknowledges that it was an informal group. In the meantime, Registrar, please, because I was just trying to go back a few pages to find something in the transcript, going back to about an hour ago, which I wanted to question the witness about, but it seems that my -- is just blocked. It's not moving. The transcript on the main monitor is scrolling perfectly, but on my laptop, it's blocked. I don't know what's happening. And it seems it's blocked here. All right. It's moving now. All right, okay. One moment, please, because I need to check something. Earlier on, I'm referring to page 30 -- bottom of page 36, the last part of page 36, and the beginning of page 37. You will recall that we were dealing with -- let's start -- page 35, rather, it went to line 20 -- 21, Mr. Wubben: [As read] "Now, with respect to the Territorial Defence, was there at that time in August already a staff functioning?" And the witness answered, "there was a Territorial Defence staff, and I've already stated that it was made up of the local commanders present in the area of Srebrenica." Question: "And who headed that staff? Who was chairing that," and then there was an objection from Mr. Jones, saying again it may be not complete -- needs to be left open, et cetera. Mr. Wubben and me, I said that that was a perfectly legitimate objection, and you asked the witness, line 16, on page -- "Did you took part of such a staff or a staff meeting?" I hope whoever is listening to me does not think that my English is that bad. "I did not take part in any of the works of the Territorial Defence staff." And then the question was: "Was Naser Oric part of the staff?" And you answered "I don't know." And then the question was: "Can you give me the names of the local commanders and their units who formed who formed part of that staff." So we're talking of staff all the time. And then your answer was: "I will try to remember them. The units were established on the territorial principle according to the area that they were established in so that the Territorial Defence unit in Suceska was commanded by Zulfo Tursunovic. The units active in the south-east of Srebrenica municipality, namely, Kragljevode, Skenderovici, were, I believe, commanded by Nedzad Bektic, Senaid Tabakovic, and I don't recall who else was there. And the unit of the Territorial Defence in Biljega was commanded by Ahmo teach. As for the town proper of Srebrenica, there were two units, one commanded by Atif Ustic and the other commanded by Hakija Meholjic. There were also units in the south-east of Srebrenica, namely, the areas of Potocari, Pale, Likari, but I don't recall who the commanders of these units were." My question -- seems to me I've been trying --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I --well, I think one has to read on from there, because at the very next line he says: "So when I said that the staff comprise commanders of the units, I meant to say that it was a rather informal group --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: He's not talking about staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: My question is completely unrelated to whether it's formal or whether it was informal. My question is: It seems to me that, looking at what you said then and what you said now, that you were not aware whether, for example, Nedzad Bektic formed part of this loose, rather informal group of people, whether Senaid Tabakovic formed part of this informal group of people. Already, about an hour ago, you told us that you knew that they formed of that group, so how come that you're now telling us that you don't know or that you didn't know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think there may be a misunderstanding on this point. I'm speaking about a specific document. I'm not aware of any decisions in documents talking about certain people being part of the staff, or becoming members of the staff. I stayed exactly what I said; namely, there was an informal group of people comprising unit commanders who came to attend certain meetings and talked about how the town defence should best be set up. I'm not sure what its name was, whether it was called staff or not. And I know nothing about any decision of this kind in May or after. We're talking about that decision. You asked me, Did I know about that decision, and I said, I had no idea. I knew those people, but I also know that local commanders would occasionally carry, that they would come individually or in a group, all of them, and hold meetings, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm not asking you about the decision, I'm just asking you whether you were aware that these three persons, Atif Krdzic, Nedzad Bektic, and Senaid Tabakovic actually did participate in this informal group you described to us. It's not whether this document is correct or not correct. I mean, we're not dealing with that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The only thing I can tell you is that these people were commanders of the units I mentioned earlier on, and where they were situated territorially, and I can tell you that I met these people. I can't tell you whether they were part of the informal group or not, whether they did go and meet there or not. I know that the people existed and that they were commanders of those units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben, he is your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Later on, when the staff, the TO staff had been established in the second half of September, were these people functioning in these functions?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were, as commanders of local units.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I need the usher to show document P4. P4 has an ERN number 01239504.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please take a look at this document, Dr. Mujkanovic.

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: It does look like Naser Oric's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Mujkanovic, will you please read this document that is -- appears to be, from the redaction, an order, Srebrenica, 15 June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And my question relates to this order, a specific part of it under Roman I, second line: "All the local leaders are ordered to immediately commence developing the organisation and establishment of the Srebrenica TO units." After that, the names of places, up to number 9, and linkage with names are mentioned. My question is, Dr. Mujkanovic -- and again to clear to you -- to make it clear to you, it's not about the document as such, an authentication, it's about those namings of the TO and of persons involved from which you already mentioned a couple. My question is: As from your experience in August 1992, were these TOs, these local TOs organised as such?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Based on my experience from 1992, I didn't know whether they were called Territorial Defence or otherwise. I only knew that they were units organised according to a territorial principle. Now, whether they were Potocari TO or Suceska TO, I couldn't tell. At the time I only knew that units existed in the area of Suceska, Osmace, Biljega, Kragljevode, Skenderovici, and so on. Accordingly, I cannot confirm that I knew that these were TO, Potocari, Suceska, and so on. As for the latter part relating to the war hospital, I can talk about that because I -- when I arrived, Hasanovic was manager of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I apologise, Dr. Mujkanovic. My question was up to -- related to 1 up to 9, and I come back later to the issue under 10. If your experience is that those names were linked to units rather than official TO or TO staff, but if you link it -- the place to units instead of the word "TO," is it correct, is it consistent with your experience, that the persons named there had, indeed, organised or were commanders of these units?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, except for the name under item 10. I don't recall the man, Mustafa Durakovic, I never met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You mean, Dr. Mujkanovic, under 9?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Nine, yes, that's correct. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Under 10, there are, and I quote: "services attached to the Srebrenica TO." Can you confirm from your knowledge that such a war hospital had been attached to the Srebrenica TO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, he hasn't conceded at any moment that there was a Srebrenica TO. I mean, I can't suggest to you, of course, because he's your question -- your witness. You need to find an alternative way of presenting it, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is it your experience that Avdo Hasanovic had set up a war hospital?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And has that war hospital been attached to the Srebrenica armed forces?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: The hospital served both the military and civilian purposes, for all those who were wounded or injured. The doctors working therein were soldiers at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that a signal -- signals and information service was functioning who was set up by Hamed Alic?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: They are non-leading ways of asking all these questions. Was there a signals and information service? If so, who set it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, you are perfectly right, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please rephrase your question, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Was there a signals and information service functioning, in your experience?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you know Hamed Alic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How -- what can you tell us about Hamed Alic? What was he doing when you came to know him? Was he responsible for anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was perhaps one of the first ones I got to know because he was working in the post office across from the hospital together with a man by the name of Ibrahim Becirevic. He was establishing the radio links with Srebrenica and its surroundings, because sometimes the civilians had to get in touch with their relatives who were out on the ground. And that's where I met him. And I believe that he was there until mid-January 1993. After that, I never saw him again. He had allegedly left the Srebrenica enclave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Next question, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you know the name Mirsad Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that man as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: In your experience, was he linked to the organisation as mentioned under 10, sub C?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm afraid I'm going to be on my feet most this morning or this afternoon. The question is: What did Mirsad Halilovic do, if anything? Otherwise it's leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Correct. So he's put the question for you. You told us that you knew Mirsad Halilovic. Yes. What was he doing there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time I knew him, I didn't know exactly what his function was. Later on, in October/November, I got to know that he was chief of the military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Does that satisfy your curiosity, Mr. Wubben, or do you want to put further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, Your Honour, and I will finalise now -- I'm complete with this document, thank you. I will go to another issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Dr. Mujkanovic, do you recall a person named Kemal Mehmetovic?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: I knew the man, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What was his nickname?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Kemo from Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: At the time in Srebrenica, what was his function? Was he a soldier or a civilian?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't say whether he held any function. I don't believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But does that mean that you don't know whether he was a soldier?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: He was quite an odd personality. It's very difficult to say whether he was a soldier or not. The only thing I can tell you is that he did wear -- that he did carry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you recall, in the beginning of August 1992, an incident took place with a human head?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you recall any incident involving Kemal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You create difficulties for me when you put such a direct question. You can't put it the way you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But now you have --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I was not the one who linked that question with a certain person. That's the Defence counsel, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: From the context.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That's your --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: This also has nothing to do with the indictment. Perhaps Mr. Wubben should --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It does have to do with the credibility of other witnesses as well, so let's -- let me take over for a while, and then I'll Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. give him back to you. And in the meantime, try to understand what I am doing, both of you. You've told us that you did know of a certain person, Kemal Mehmetovic, that he was also known as Kemo from Pale; that he carried arms, but that, to you, you are not in a position to tell us that he was a soldier or that he had any specific function. How many times did you see him, in Srebrenica, to start with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd seen him many times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, what were you going to tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He'd usually walk around the town, had this small truck that he drove. He was very often intoxicated, drunk, of a very bad temper, picked fights with people very easily, and that's why people shirked away from him, avoided him. He was actually quite a difficult personality in terms of his mindset.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was there any particular event, when you saw Kemal, that has stuck in your memory that you could tell us about? Some special occasion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure what event you have in mind. There were always incidents in his vicinity. Not a day would go by without him skidding the truck off to a ditch or walking the town drunk, provoking people, picking on people, so that you would have to actually specify the event that you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, but was there any particular occasion which was quite out of the ordinary - it's not just his usual behaviour, but it's something beyond -- which goes beyond that - that struck you as something exceptional?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably you have the following event in mind: In early August, immediately after my arrival in Srebrenica, at the time I practically didn't know who he was, there was a truckload of wounded people who were brought to the hospital and I wanted to conduct my triage according to the degree of urgency based on their wounds, because there was a large batch of persons who came across a minefield. Many amputations had to be carried out, and we had to prioritise among the wounded to see who ought to be operated on first. There were many people in front of the hospital, trying to find out if there were any relatives or members of their family among the wounded. That was when Kemal showed up. He was perhaps some 20 or 30 metres away from the hospital, and I noticed him in the crowd. He showed up holding a human head by the hair. Later on, I heard this story talked about in the town, that he had brought a human head. I could not, with my own eyes, ascertain that it was, indeed, a human head. I was looking at him from about a 30-metre distance. I believe he was responsible for another incident after this one, and then he left the Srebrenica enclave. I believe it was sometime at the end of 1992 that he left Srebrenica, but I don't know where he had gone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What other incident was he responsible for? Can you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Reportedly, there was a bloody vendetta for some sort of an incident dating from before, a vengeance of a sort, where he killed a man. There was a beating involved. I'm telling you what I heard, not what I saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right, yes, he's back to you, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I notice also the time. Is it scheduled to have a break at a quarter past 12 or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have seven minutes, but as I always do, I invite the parties to select the right moment for a break. It's up to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I think this is the right moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, okay. Twenty-five minutes

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Wubben, and I will invite Madam Vidovic or Mr. Jones, I would like you to approach. I would like to tell you something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Wubben, one moment, because I must have touched something here. All right, okay. No problem. Let's continue, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to ask the assistance of the usher. Document P6, ERN number 01239515.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please, Dr. Mujkanovic, will you take a look at this document.

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: The first half of the signature is covered by the stamp; therefore, I cannot say with certainty that this is Naser Oric's signature. The second half, though, looks much like his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Dr. Mujkanovic, this is a document with the heading "Srebrenica TO," and the date is the 3rd of September, 1992. In September 1992, I take it that you were in Srebrenica. Were you at that time familiar -- did you know this decision or a kind of decision like this?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not receiving any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have a technical problem. Could I ask you to repeat your question. Maybe it's already solved. Are you receiving interpretation now? Nothing. So it's not solved, so there's no point in repeating the question. I will keep on talking for a while until ... Are you receiving interpretation now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Wubben, sorry for that interruption.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honour, where to start, so I'll start from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think because obviously there was -- the number, the channel number, had been changed so he couldn't have possibly received any interpretations -- interpretation from the very moment we started after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But he was answering your questions before, so I don't know what happened. He has told us so far that he cannot really recognise the signature, although the part which is not superimposed by the stamp seems to look similar to that of Naser Oric. And then you asked him to have a look at the text of this document, and you said: "Dr. Mujkanovic, this is a document with the heading "Srebrenica TO," and the date is the 3rd of September, 1992. In September 1992, I take it that you were in Srebrenica. Were you at that time familiar -- did you know this decision or a kind of decision like this?" I have repeated verbatim what you had asked the witness. So that is the question that you need to answer now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not familiar with this kind of decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you know, as of the -- of September 1992, the naming of, and I quote, "staff of the armed forces of Srebrenica, the Srebrenica armed forces staff"?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: It was only once I became a member of the operations staff of the armed forces of Srebrenica, in the second half of September, was I aware of what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: We will come to that issue later on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Usher, will you assist me with the following document: P176, ERN number 03720933.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Dr. Mujkanovic, would you please take a look at that document.

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: I've had a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Dr. Mujkanovic, do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: The first part is covered by the stamp; it's illegible. The second part looks like Naser Oric's signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: The wording of the document reads, in the head, "Srebrenica Armed Forces Staff," the date, "Srebrenica, 3rd September 1992," and naming the decision, "The operations staff of the Srebrenica armed forces shall be established as the constituent part of the Srebrenica armed forces staff." Is that decision, like that, consistent with your experience at that time, in September 1992, in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: In mid-September, the second half of September, the operations staff of Srebrenica was set up and I became a member. That's what I know. This is the first time I see this decision, and I wasn't familiar with this decision at the time. I do know that Osman Osmanovic was the chief of the operations staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And what you know about Osman Osmanovic, that is your experience from September 1992.

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Following --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because he said -- the witness said this is the first time he is seeing this decision. Are you sure it's the first time you're seeing this decision?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw this decision when the OTP showed me a copy. At the time I said that I'd never seen it before. I'm just repeating what I've already stated. That was when I first saw this decision, of course, in that case, this being the second time. My understanding was -- you asked about me seeing this decision prior to the last several days that I've spent here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, because you said this is the first time you're seeing this decision, and I have reason to believe that this is not the first time you're seeing this decision; that, as you said, you were shown this decision before. Do you remember, when was that, whether it was days or months ago or years ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not years ago. I think the first time this was shown me was in June last year, and then it was shown again some days ago. But I thought your question was to the effect whether I'd seen this decision while I was still in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, no, it's because you said this is the first time you're seeing this decision. So basically, I take it, this is the third time you're seeing it; it was shown to you in June, it was shown to you some days ago, and you're seeing it now, today; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I would like to move now to Exhibit number P79, and I've been informed that the registrar will provide a copy of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please, Dr. Mujkanovic, take a look at this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why? We have an English translation. When it was tendered way back, I don't know when, it was tendered with an English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You're correct, Your Honour. It should be the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but we have the B/C/S version as well, so what's wrong? I am not understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's move ahead. But for your information, Mr. Wubben, I know that you are using supposedly what you refer to as the original, but in our records, we have this document in B/C/S and in English, and it's marked, as you said, P79.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you for this confirmation. And I add to it, Your Honour, the ERN number 02078514.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Dr. Mujkanovic, did you have a look at this document?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: This document reads in the heading "Operations Staff Srebrenica," and dated "Srebrenica, 19 September 1992." In short, it starts with "Draft Decision," it is -- where it is signed, it has the reference, chief of the operations staff of the armed forces, Osman Osmanovic. Do you know Osman Osmanovic?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is it your experience that he was, in fact, in September, indeed, the chief of the operations staff of the armed forces, if so?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, will you please take a look further at the redaction of this document, and there is a listing 1 up to 11.

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: I've read this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Above that there is a sentence that ends, and I quote, "proposes that the operations staff of the armed forces in Srebrenica consists of the following departments and people." Now, my question to you is: When -- upon -- sorry, upon reading the names and the linked departments or one organ and one functioning as a recording secretary, is it your experience in your times in Srebrenica that these persons linked to those specific parts were functioning in the operations staff?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So to be specific, the persons mentioned 1 up to 11, that is, to your knowledge, from September 1992, functioning within that operations staff?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Does that include that the person mentioned as Mustafa Salihovic was, indeed, recording as the secretary of such a meeting, or don't you know?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: He was there at the meetings I attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And my question is: Was he recording at that meeting, or don't you know?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean, "recording"?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Taking minutes or writing down specific parts, what was discussed or whatever, to record -- to make records.

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, by hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: The following -- next document, usher, please, is number P8. P8 with the ERN number 01239518.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: This is a decision, Dr. Mujkanovic, and I'll read out the head now: "Srebrenica Municipality Armed Forces War Presidency, Srebrenica, 14th of October 1992," and then there's a decision on naming and appointing "Osman Osmanovic Srebrenica is hereby named and appointed as the chief of staff of OS," armed forces. And then under 5: "This decision comes into effect on the day of its adoption. The named and appointed person must report immediately to the commander of the armed forces." When it comes to your experience in Srebrenica, from the time you were there, is it, to your knowledge, an experience that the named person, Osman Osmanovic, reported to the commander of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: I assume so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What do you mean by "assume so," because either you have experience as such report or you don't know.

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: I really can't say whether he reported to the commander of the armed forces. I assume he did. But Osman did not report to me to say who he had reported to. I really can't answer the question, whether he reported to anyone, including the commander of the armed forces. I don't know. I did say that I certainly assumed that he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you know who was in the chain of command above Osman Osmanovic?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Above Osman Osmanovic in the chain of command, there was the commander of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And who was at the time the commander of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the armed forces at the time was Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: May I, Your Honour, just on this document. My learned friend says it's headed "Srebrenica Municipality Armed Forces War Presidency." In fact, it says "Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, opstina Srebrenica," so Srebrenica municipality, "War Presidency." So the heading itself doesn't say anything about the armed forces. The "OS" might have misled my learned friend, being "Opstina Srebrenica" rather than "oruzane snage," armed forces, but it's clear from the Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for that observation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I would also point out that this is signed by Hajrudin Avdic, president of the War Presidency, to get that onto the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for that observation, Mr. Jones, which is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I can confirm, Your Honour, that that's what is meant by the OS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is also confirmation of it by the first line of the text. Again, you see "Opstina Srebrenica." Yes, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: The following document is P84, and I would like the assistance of the usher to hand over to Dr. Mujkanovic a document. It is a memo pad under the ERN number 02115040.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please take a look at this memo pad.

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Are you familiar with any use of a memo pad or a war diary like this within a TO, an army or ...

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll try to be crystal clear about this. I have seen this document before, but when I did was the first time. I did not know that there was a document that talked about this writing, diary, whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Mujkanovic, if you look --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Dr. Mujkanovic, if you take a look at the book when it is -- the diary when it is closed, totally closed, please, will you close the diary? Thank you. If you take a look at it, are you familiar with memo pads or war diaries or diaries used in armed forces who looks like this, this appearance?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not. This is a notebook. It was used by the TO of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you mean that a book like that, a war diary like that, was commonly used, as such, in the army?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, can we place it, a little bit, the cover I mean, on the ELMO so that the public can see what we're talking about. Yes, and can you open it up a little bit, please, just the first page. Okay, you can remove it now. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Dr. Mujkanovic, will you please go from the page, in the B/C/S version you have in front of you, 02115042, and then page by page, to 46, the last two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I suppose that's in the original or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That's in the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And what's the equivalent in English?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Sorry, not 010, 710.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, if you take a look at the B/C/S, ERN number 02115042 and 43, and that's English ERN 06 and 07, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: There is on 07 -- and that's my English version, and Dr. Mujkanovic, on your version, it is -- it's the version started with -- it is 42, and I quote, and I hope you will see it, please confirm: "Second meeting of the armed forces operations staff." It's 44, Dr. Mujkanovic. Is that correct? Do you see a heading like that on ERN 02115044?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, in the page -- on the page with the ERN number, in English, 08, and in B/C/S, Dr. Mujkanovic, ERN 02115046, we see, and I quote, heading started with, "Minutes, 3 October 1992."

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: When you earlier referred to a meeting you participated in, did you participate in a meeting of the operations staff on the 3rd of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please go to ERN 02115044, Dr. Mujkanovic, and 707 for the English. There is a reference to a second meeting, as already confirmed to you, of the armed forces operations staff. This second meeting, did you participate in such a second meeting of the armed forces operations staff as it is possible before the 3rd of October, 1992, in the order of the diary?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now we go, prior to that second meeting, to ERN 02115042, that's the B/C/S, and the English version is 03090706 [Realtime transcript read in error "00790776"].

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did attend that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So is that meeting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because for the record, it -- the English version is said to be 00790776, the last three digits are 706, or should be 706 and 776. Yes, go ahead, Mr. Wubben, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did you attend that meeting?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is it correct that there were -- at the meeting you experienced, there were around nine members?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember how many there were, but it was a meeting of the staff that I attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, is it correct that -- if you recall, of course, can you confirm that Osmanovic, Nedret, and the other names mentioned in the first paragraph, took part in a discussion?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Whenever I attended, I took part in the discussions, so that much is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can you confirm, as in the minutes further on, the name Osman appeared, and there is a reference to, a military corps [sic] must be formed. Do you recall that issue at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: A military corps? I don't really understand the term, the terminology.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I take that for an answer, thank you. I will now proceed on the part of the staff members. There is a listing 1 up to 10, including a kind of bold arrow, there are persons named, and there are, well, units or departments. Please read them.

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is it your experience that the staff members, indeed, performed such duties or were linked to these kind of functions or departments?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: After the establishment of the operations staff, all the staff members worked in the different areas they were assigned to, as, indeed, written down here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Under 1 up to 10.

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, please allow me to repeat my prior question, because I was -- noticed that when I asked the witness that a person called Osman was referred to -- that a military corps must be formed, that, indeed, it had been noted as corps instead of court, with a T. So please allow me to ask that question again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly. And if need be, we will have the first page of the diary, or whatever you call it, on the ELMO so that, if there is a difficulty in the interpretation, we will be able to refer to the specific entry. Usher, could you put on the ELMO, please, ERN 042, 042, which is, I suppose, the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please, Dr. Mujkanovic, look at the text under paragraph 1. They are referring to the name Osman, and then "a military court must be formed." Do you recall that an issue like that has been discussed?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: At this particular meeting, following the establishment of the operations staff, as indeed contained in these minutes, there was a discussion about the establishment of units and about the organisation of the armed forces in the area of Srebrenica, according to the military doctrine, in other words, that platoons, companies, battalions, and brigades are to be established, and whatever, of course, came under and was entailed by the establishment of such units. There was also discussion about the establishment of a military court.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And what do you mean by military doctrine?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: I mean to say that the units had to be established the way I said, platoon, company, battalion, brigade, and the other military organisations that come under it, up to the strength of a brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: All right. Now, what had been said about this military court, Dr. Mujkanovic?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing else was said other than that a military court had to be established as a component part of setting up military structures in the area of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, my question is: We already have read through a part of this page 42. Have you also took a look at page within -- 43?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've taken a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can I take it that page -- the two pages, 42 and ending up with 43 of the war diary, are an accurate reflection of the minutes you took part of?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment before you answer, because I don't quite know how this was translated to you. Actually, I looked at you, Mr. Wubben, because I heard you say "an accurate reflection of the minutes you took part of." I think you meant to say "the meeting you took part of," and I don't know how that was translated. So we're talking of the meeting, and whether the minutes, what are purported to be minutes, what you're reading now, reflects accurately what went on during that meeting that you attended, Dr. Mujkanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I would like to move on to another document, P177, a decision, the 7th of February, 1993. That's ERN number 037209334.

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: The first question is: Do you recognise the signature at the down end? There are several signatures. One signature, and I quote in English, "Srebrenica Armed Forces Commander," that signature, do you recognise that signature?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: The signature is quite illegible, and I cannot state with any certainty that it does look like his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: This is a document with the heading "War Presidency of the subregion Srebrenica, Vlasenica, Bratunac, and Zvornik municipalities," dated Srebrenica, 7 February 1993. My question is: In the further heading of the first part of this decision, it is referring to a War Presidency of the subregion and the staff of the subregion, the armed forces. Are you familiar with this subregion, to your experience?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: I heard of the expression.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But, to your knowledge, you don't know about -- you can't tell the Judges about the functioning of the subregion, or the area involved?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: I know approximately that there were certain activities taking place geared to provide an effective defence for Srebrenica, Vlasenica, Bratunac, and Zvornik, in late 1992 and early 1993, and that at the time there was a discussion about grouping, amalgamating, units and setting up a single authority for the area, in order for the human resources important for the defence of the area, as well as the materiel and technical equipment, to be utilised fully. Now, whether this subregion was actually established or not, I cannot tell you because I never really learnt whether it was established and whether it actually functioned as such. I think that this was rather an idea of how to use the human and materiel and technical potentials in the area for the defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Had this idea been established in such a way that decisions were made upon it, to execute, to implement, that idea?

utterances.speaker: NEDRET MUJKANOVIC
utterances.text: I've said that I didn't know whether it was formed, and I said that this Salihovic was president of the War Presidency of the subregion because I know that at the time he was the one in charge for security and intelligence in the staff. But I couldn't really give you a certain judgement as to whether the subregion functioned or not. I was telling you that this was an idea present in 1993 when it was thought that this whole area should be united into a single region in order to increase its efficiency.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, my next issue is a different issue, so it seems reasonable to stop here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will stop here for the day. I think it must have been tiring for everyone, not least, of course, yourself, Mr. Wubben. We'll reconvene tomorrow. Is it -- are we still working in this courtroom tomorrow? You think you can check whether there is any other availability, just in case? No. But keep checking. In case we can transfer to some other courtroom, we'll do our best. Dr. Mujkanovic, we have to stop here for today because we must make the courtroom available for another case which will sit in the afternoon. We will meet again tomorrow morning. Thank you. In the meantime, it's important that you do not contact, or let anyone contact you in relation to the matters that you are testifying upon, okay? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 15th day of February, 2005, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.42 p.m.,
